answer: Bind each agent to a distinct model fingerprint. Step 1: at enrollment the agent registers the hash of its own fine-tuned model weights. Step 2: every day the network sends a random prompt and the agent must answer within 60 seconds using that exact model. Step 3: two identities sharing one weight hash both get burned. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 distinct 8-billion-parameter models, about $40 GPU each, so $40,000 plus 16 TB of storage. Like an orchard where a zephyr carries each tree's own scent, an ember of real work glows in every genuine fingerprint while copies smell of nothing.
